project.name: Elrics
project.description: A full-stack Mission Control dashboard that combines a Next.js 16 frontend, Supabase platform services, and a Django REST Framework sidecar API.
project.architecture_style: Hybrid full-stack architecture with a shared PostgreSQL database

presentation_summary.django_integration: I integrated Django REST Framework as a sidecar backend service. It connects directly to the same Supabase PostgreSQL database as the Next.js application and exposes standard REST CRUD endpoints for users, products, and todos.
why_django_is_useful: It provides a structured, framework-based REST API for consumers that prefer HTTP endpoints over direct Supabase client access.
DRF ModelViewSets, serializers, and router-based URLs make CRUD features consistent and easy to extend with validation, permissions, business rules, reporting, or third-party integrations.
It separates future server-side business logic from the frontend while still allowing Supabase to handle authentication, realtime updates, and database operations.
Django models are unmanaged, so Supabase remains the only owner of database schema changes and there is no migration conflict between the two backends.
CORS configuration lets the Next.js frontend call the Django API during local development.
presentation_summary.important_design_note: The current Next.js dashboard primarily uses the Supabase client directly for authentication, realtime subscriptions, and todo operations. Django is an additional API layer, ready for API-first clients or server-side workflows; it is not a replacement for Supabase.

responsibilities: Renders the Mission Control dashboard using the App Router.
Manages client-side authentication UI and session state.
Runs todo CRUD, realtime, storage, and diagnostic UI flows through Supabase clients.
Refreshes Supabase authentication cookies through middleware.
Exposes browsable and JSON REST endpoints.
Implements list, retrieve, create, update, and delete operations through DRF ModelViewSets.
Serializes and validates API payloads for users, products, and todos.
Adds UUID and created-at values when records are created through Django.
Owns the public database schema, SQL migrations, seed data, and row-level-security policies.
Provides browser-safe authentication and realtime capabilities to the Next.js application.
Runs database migration, seed, reset, health, connectivity, and authentication checks.
Provides repeatable operational and test workflows.

data_flow.path: Browser -> Next.js dashboard -> Supabase Auth/PostgREST/Realtime -> Supabase PostgreSQL
data_flow.use_case: Interactive authentication, live todo CRUD, realtime updates, storage checks, and telemetry.

data_flow.path: Browser or external client -> Django REST Framework -> Django ORM unmanaged models -> Supabase PostgreSQL
data_flow.use_case: Standard REST integration, backend validation, and future server-side business workflows.

data_flow.path: SQL files and TypeScript migration scripts -> Supabase PostgreSQL
data_flow.use_case: Creates and evolves database objects outside Django migrations.

database_strategy.django_model_policy: All Django models use managed = false. Django maps to existing tables but never creates, alters, or drops them.
database_strategy.security: Row Level Security is configured in Supabase SQL. Django connects directly to PostgreSQL, so production deployments should add DRF authentication and permission policies before exposing write endpoints publicly.

root..env: Runtime credentials; excluded from version control.
root.supabase/: Database schema, seed data, and SQL migrations.
root.scripts/: TypeScript operational, migration, and test scripts.

src.app/: App Router layout, page, and global styles.
src.components/: Dashboard, authentication, status, modal, and CRUD UI components.
src.hooks/: Reusable Supabase, profile, and authentication React hooks.
src.lib/: Supabase browser/server clients, environment validation, typed database models, and auth helpers.
src.middleware.ts: Refreshes Supabase user sessions for matching Next.js requests.

backend.elrics_api/settings.py: Database, Django, DRF, and CORS settings.
backend.api/serializers.py: DRF serializers for request validation and response formatting.
backend.api/views.py: CRUD ModelViewSets and server-side record defaults.
backend.api/urls.py: DRF router registrations for users, products, and todos.

supabase.schema.sql: Base PostgreSQL schema, RLS policies, and realtime publication setup.
supabase.migrations/: Versioned SQL schema changes, including social-feed and comment migrations.

frontend_social_feed_platform.purpose: A standalone static social-feed frontend prototype. It uses plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and communicates with Supabase through its JavaScript service layer.

pages.feed.html: Main social-feed page for viewing and interacting with posts.
pages.README.md: Setup and usage notes for the standalone frontend.

css.styles.css: Global visual styles, typography, colours, and base rules.
css.layout.css: Page grid, navigation, content-area, and responsive layout structure.
css.components.css: Reusable UI styles for cards, buttons, forms, modals, toasts, and feed elements.

javascript.app.js: Shared application bootstrap and common client-side initialization.

pages.login.js: Login-page behavior and authentication submission flow.
pages.register.js: Registration-page behavior and account creation flow.
pages.feed.js: Feed loading, post interactions, and feed-page behavior.
pages.profile.js: Profile loading, editing, and profile-page behavior.

services.supabase-config.js: Supabase client configuration and connection setup.
services.api.js: Data-access functions used by pages to communicate with Supabase services.

components.comments.js: Reusable comment display and interaction behavior.
components.toast.js: Transient success, warning, and error notifications.

utils.validation.js: Reusable client-side form and input validation.
utils.helpers.js: Shared utility functions used across pages and components.

frontend_social_feed_platform.frontend_flow: HTML page -> page-specific JavaScript -> shared API service -> Supabase. Shared components and utilities support consistent UI behavior across each page.

future_extension_points: Add DRF authentication and object-level permission classes tied to Supabase JWT verification.
Move complex business rules, batch operations, webhooks, and third-party integrations into Django service modules.
Add API versioning, rate limiting, OpenAPI documentation, and production-specific CORS and allowed-host configuration.
Have the Next.js frontend call Django endpoints selectively where server-owned rules are required.
